## 11. What changed from version 1.0

| Area | Version 1.0 (from 1 January 2025) | Version 2.0 (from 1 July 2026) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meals and subsistence | £35 a day | £40 a day |
| Hotel, London | £180 a night | £200 a night |
| Hotel, rest of the UK | £120 a night | £130 a night |
| Hotel, Lisbon or Dublin | €170 a night | €180 a night |
| Hotel, other EU cities | €150 a night | €160 a night |
| Client entertainment | £60 a head | £75 a head |
| Receipts | Itemised receipt for expenses over £50 | Itemised receipt for every expense above £25 |
| Claim deadline | 60 days | 30 days |
| Alcohol with meals | Allowed within the daily limit | Not reimbursed, except client entertainment |
| First class rail | Not reimbursed | Allowed for journeys over 3 hours, booked 7 days ahead, at most £30 above standard |

The hotel and meals limits were raised after the Finance review of 2025 travel spend found that 41% of London hotel bookings went over the £180 limit with approval. The receipt threshold was lowered to meet the audit recommendation of February 2026.

chunks.text:
### 4.2 Hotels

The nightly limit covers the room and taxes. It does not cover the minibar, room service beyond the meals limit, films, laundry for stays under 5 nights, or late checkout. If you stay with friends or family instead of a hotel, you may claim £25 a night towards a thank-you gift or meal, with a receipt.

For a stay that spans the change of policy, each night is paid at the limit in force on that night.

### 4.1 Meals and subsistence

You can claim meals when you travel overnight on business, or when you work away from your usual office for more than 10 hours in a day. The daily limit covers breakfast, lunch, dinner and soft drinks. A reasonable amount of alcohol with an evening meal is allowed within the daily limit.

If breakfast is included in your hotel rate, the daily limit stays the same.

chunks.text:
## 3. Gifts and hospitality

| Situation | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Gift worth £50 or less | You may accept. No need to record it. |
| Gift worth more than £50 | Record it in the gifts and hospitality register within 7 days. Your manager decides whether you can keep it. |
| Hospitality up to £150 a head | Allowed with your manager's approval, recorded in the register |
| Hospitality over £150 a head | Needs Compliance approval before you accept |
| Cash, vouchers, gift cards | Never accept, whatever the amount |
| Anything from a supplier or partner during a tender, negotiation or renewal with them | Decline it |

Gifts you give follow the same £50 limit. Hospitality you give, such as client entertainment, follows the limit per head and the approval rules in the Travel and Expenses Policy, not the table above. Never give anything of value to a public official, including a regulator, without Compliance approval.

## 9. Liability

Each party's total liability in a contract year is limited to 150% of the charges paid or payable in the previous 12 months. Liability for breach of clause 7 or of confidentiality is limited separately to £5,000,000. Nothing limits liability for fraud, death or personal injury.

### 3.2 Air

Fly economy for any flight under 6 hours. Premium economy is allowed for flights of 6 hours or more with head of department approval. Checked baggage is reimbursed when you travel for 3 nights or more, or when you carry equipment.

chunks.text:
## 3. Booking travel

Book all flights, rail and hotels through the travel booking portal on the intranet. The portal applies the limits in section 4 and sends the booking to your line manager for approval. Bookings made outside the portal are only reimbursed if the portal could not offer a comparable option, and you must say why in the claim.

Book at least 14 days ahead where you can. Last-minute bookings over the limits need written approval from your head of department.

chunks.text:
## 2. Principles

- Spend company money as carefully as you would spend your own.

- Choose the cheapest option that still gets the job done. Time matters too: a cheaper flight that costs you a day is not cheaper.

- Get approval before you book travel, not after.

- Claim only what you actually spent, once, with the evidence this policy asks for.

- The limits below are maximums, not allowances. If you spend less, claim less.

chunks.text:
## 1. Annual leave

### 1.1 Entitlement

The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December.

| Office | Annual leave | Public holidays | Winter closure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| London | 27 days | England bank holidays (8 in 2026) | 3 days |
| Lisbon | 25 days | Portuguese national holidays, the Lisbon municipal holiday, and Carnaval | 3 days |
| Dublin | 25 days | Irish public holidays (10 in 2026) | 3 days |

You get one extra day of annual leave after 3 years' service and a second after 5 years, to a maximum of 2 extra days. Part-time employees get the same entitlement pro rata. If you join or leave during the year, your entitlement is pro rata to the days you work in that year, rounded up to the nearest half day.

Travel standard class. First class is allowed for a single journey of more than 3 hours if you book it at least 7 days ahead and it costs no more than £30 above the standard fare.

## 5. Expenses

Kestrel pays back reasonable costs you incur on company business. The limits, receipt rules and how to claim are in the Travel and Expenses Policy in /HR/Policies. Always check the version in force on the date you spend the money; this handbook does not repeat the limits.

## 7. Kitchens and post

- Kitchens are on every floor in London. Fruit arrives on Monday and Thursday, and there is breakfast on Tuesdays from 08:30.

- Label food in the fridges. Fridges are cleared every Friday at 16:00.

- Post arrives at reception at about 10:00 and 14:00. Personal parcels are allowed, but please collect them within 2 days.

- Fines, penalties and parking tickets

- Personal travel insurance (the company policy covers business trips)

- Gym, spa and leisure charges

## 2. London: Harrow Yard

### 2.1 Getting there

Old Street station (Northern line) is a 6 minute walk. Liverpool Street (Elizabeth line, Central line and national rail) is 12 minutes. There are 40 bike spaces and 6 showers in the basement, entered from the side door on Paul's Alley.

First aiders in London are Ella Brooks, Hannah Kim and Luis Ortega. First aid kits are next to every kitchen, and the defibrillator is at reception on floor 3. Report any accident at work to Ella Brooks the same day, however small.
